title: 489. Hundred Years' War: Bloodbath at Agincourt (Part 3)

sentences.en: This story shall the good man teach his son, and Crispin Crispian shall ne'er go by from this day to the ending of the world, but we in it shall be remembered, we few,
sentences.zh: 此人当以这番话教导儿子，克里斯潘节永不被人遗忘，从今天直到世界末日，我们都将留在其中，我们这寥寥数人，

sentences.en: we happy few, we band of brothers, for he today that sheds his blood with me shall be my brother.
sentences.zh: 我们这幸存的寥寥数人，我们这兄弟连，因为今天与我一同浴血奋战的人，就是我的兄弟。

sentences.en: Be he ne'er so vile, this day shall gentle his condition, and gentlemen in England now abed, shall think themselves a curse they were not here,
sentences.zh: 无论他多么卑微，这一天都将提升他的身份，而如今躺在英格兰温床上的绅士们，会觉得自己没有来到这里是个诅咒，

sentences.en: and hold their manhoods cheap whilst any speaks that fought with us upon St Crispin's day.
sentences.zh: 每当有人谈起我们在圣克里斯潘节并肩作战时，他们就会觉得自己的人格分文不值。

sentences.en: That is stirring stuff Tom, it's the most famous speech on a battlefield ever written, one of the most famous speeches in English history, or English literary history anyway,
sentences.zh: 真是振奋人心啊，汤姆，这是有史以来最著名的战场演讲，无论如何也是英国历史乃至英国文学史上最著名的演讲之一，

sentences.en: it's Henry V at the Battle of Agincourt, I know you love the Kenneth Branagh version,
sentences.zh: 这就是阿金库尔战役中的《亨利五世》，我知道你很喜欢肯尼斯·布拉纳的版本，

sentences.en: you've been watching it on a loop on YouTube to inspire yourself for today's episode on Agincourt, Branagh does it brilliantly doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 你一直在YouTube上单曲循环，为今天关于阿金库尔的节目寻找灵感，布拉纳演得真是绝妙，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does it with a kind of rising lilt.
sentences.zh: 他用了一种带有上扬声调的语调来演绎。

sentences.en: He does, and his production, I remember at the time, his production was seen as a groundbreaking film version, because it broke with the sort of technicolour,
sentences.zh: 确实如此，而且我记得当时他的作品被视为一部具有突破性的电影版本，因为它打破了那种特艺七彩的、

sentences.en: slightly manicured look of Olivier's Henry V, and he was down in the mud wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 略带修饰的劳伦斯·奥利弗版《亨利五世》的风格，他当时可是落入泥潭了不是吗？

sentences.en: A soldier among soldiers.
sentences.zh: 士兵之中的士兵。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Olivier's one was very deliberately done as being patriotic, it was made in 1944,
sentences.zh: 对，奥利弗的版本是非常刻意地表现爱国主义，它拍摄于1944年，

sentences.en: all the awkward bits in Shakespeare's play that makes Henry V as a hero slightly ambivalent were cut, and Branagh's as you say, I mean there's lots of mud, there's lots of rain,
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚戏剧中所有让亨利五世作为英雄显得有些矛盾尴尬的片段都被删掉了，而正如你所说，布拉纳的版本，我是说有很多泥泞，有很多雨，

sentences.en: which is very authentic to the actual battle, but in that speech he really goes in hard.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合实际战役的情况，但在那段演讲中，他真的演得很带劲。

sentences.en: It's absolutely thrilling, and we've talked about this before, it's undoubtedly the reason why Agincourt blazes in the imagination of the English,
sentences.zh: 这绝对令人激动，我们以前也讨论过，毫无疑问，这就是为什么阿金库尔战役在英国人的想象中闪耀着光芒，

sentences.en: perhaps more brightly than any other victory won by an English army.
sentences.zh: 或许比英国军队赢得的任何其他胜利都要耀眼。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 对，我想确实如此。

sentences.en: But it's not just down to Shakespeare, so it's clear right from the beginning, long before Shakespeare,
sentences.zh: 但这不仅归功于莎士比亚，从一开始就很明显，早在莎士比亚之前很久，

sentences.en: that the English do see Agincourt as being exceptional in a way that neither Cressy nor Poitier had been.
sentences.zh: 英国人就已经把阿金库尔视为非同寻常的胜利，这是克雷西或普瓦捷所不具备的。

sentences.en: And in Henry V, that great speech, which you read so powerfully, Dominic, is prompted by a lament from one of Henry's peers from Westmoreland, that they're terribly outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 而在《亨利五世》中，那段由你充满力量地朗读的伟大演讲，是由亨利的一位同僚威斯特摩兰的感叹引发的，他们的人数实在太少了。

sentences.en: So Westmoreland, you know, he's looking out at the French, and he says, oh, that we now had here but one ten thousand of those men in England that do no work today.
sentences.zh: 所以威斯特摩兰，你知道的，他看着法军，然后说，哦，但愿现在这里有那一万个今天无所事事的英格兰人。

sentences.en: And Henry replies, I pray thee, wish not one man more.
sentences.zh: 而亨利回答说，我求你，一个都不要再求了。

sentences.en: If we die, that's, you know, we don't want any more, and if we win, then the glory is all the greater.
sentences.zh: 如果我们战死，那就是，你知道的，我们不需要更多人，如果我们获胜，那么荣耀就会更加伟大。

sentences.en: And the thing is that Shakespeare is not making this up.
sentences.zh: 关键在于莎士比亚并非凭空捏造。

sentences.en: So this is reported by the chaplain, who is one of the two combatants on the English side who have written accounts of Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 这是随军牧师记载的，他是英方留下阿金库尔战役文字记录的两名参战者之一。

sentences.en: And the chaplain reports a knight as making the same complaint that Westmoreland makes in Shakespeare's play.
sentences.zh: 牧师记录说，一名骑士发出了与莎士比亚戏剧中威斯特摩兰相同的抱怨。

sentences.en: And Henry's retort, according to his chaplain, is I would not, even if I could, have a single man more than I do.
sentences.zh: 而根据他的牧师记载，亨利的顶撞是：即使我能，我也不要比现在多哪怕一个人。

sentences.en: But there's a slightly different kind of emphasis in Henry's words as reported by the chaplain.
sentences.zh: 但牧师所记载的亨利的话中，着重点略有不同。

sentences.en: Because Henry says, do you not believe that the Almighty, with these his humble few,
sentences.zh: 因为亨利说，难道你们不相信全能的上帝，凭借着这区区少数的谦卑之人，

sentences.en: is able to overcome the opposing arrogance of the French who boast of their great number and their own strength?
sentences.zh: 能够战胜法国人那自吹自擂的人多势众和狂妄自大吗？

sentences.en: So the emphasis there is on the idea that the victory proves God's backing for Henry.
sentences.zh: 所以那里的重点在于，这场胜利证明了上帝对亨利的支持。

sentences.en: And this is clearly hugely important to Henry because the battle for him is a kind of teSt.
sentences.zh: 这显然对亨利至关重要，因为对他来说，这场战役是一次考验。

sentences.en: He's putting his claim to the French throne in the balance.
sentences.zh: 他正在将自己对法国王位的声索押在天平上。

sentences.en: And isn't it interesting how those themes that are hit both by the chaplain's account and by Shakespeare, they resonate so deeply in English history.
sentences.zh: 而且不觉得很有趣吗，那些在牧师的记载和莎士比亚的作品中都出现的主题，在英国历史上产生了如此深刻的共鸣。

sentences.en: The idea of the humble few against a massively superior army.
sentences.zh: 以区区少数对抗庞大优势军队的概念。

sentences.en: The arrogance of the French, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 法国人的傲慢，诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got the Band of Brothers that we mentioned before that Nelson was inspired by, the idea of the few that obviously, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们之前提到过纳尔逊所受启发的兄弟连，显而易见，你知道的，

sentences.en: Churchill and whatnot played with in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔和其他人在第二次世界大战中也运用了这种“少数人”的概念。

sentences.en: But at the time, I guess that also reflects a wider political, geographical reality that France is much larger, economically more powerful, has far greater manpower than England.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，我想这也反映了一个更广泛的政治和地理现实，即法国比英格兰大得多，经济更强大，人力资源丰富得多。

sentences.en: And so the English, the sense of themselves as being the underdogs, it's very Russia and Ukraine or something, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因此，英国人将自己视为弱者的心态，非常像俄乌战争或者别的什么，不是吗？

sentences.en: They've launched an incursion into the enemy territory.
sentences.zh: 他们对敌方领土发动了突袭。

sentences.en: They're massively outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 他们的人数处于绝对劣势。

sentences.en: But they are absolutely convinced that right and justice are on their side,
sentences.zh: 但他们坚信真理和正义在他们这一边，

sentences.en: even though presumably the people living in the surrounding French villages might see things rather differently.
sentences.zh: 尽管周围法国村庄里生活的居民可能会有相当不同的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah, might have a slightly different perspective.
sentences.zh: 是的，可能会有稍微不同的视角。

sentences.en: But they capitalise on it, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将看到的，他们利用了这一点。

sentences.en: So they benefit from it too.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也从中受益。

sentences.en: It also reflects the fact that clearly for the English, when they crest this hill, which we described at the end of the last episode,
sentences.zh: 这也反映了一个事实，很显然，对英国人来说，当他们登上我们在上一集结尾时描述的那座小山，

sentences.en: and they look out and they see the French forces in front of them, it's terrifying.
sentences.zh: 放眼望去，看到眼前的法军时，那是极其可怕的。

sentences.en: So again, to quote Henry's chaplain, he sees the French cavalry thundering from all directions to block their path.
sentences.zh: 因此，再次引用亨利牧师的话，他看到法国骑兵从四面八方雷鸣般冲来，挡住了他们的去路。

sentences.en: And he says they're like a countless swarm of locusts.
sentences.zh: 他说他们就像数不清的蝗虫群。

sentences.en: And he has no doubt that the English are absolutely massively outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 他毫不怀疑英国人在人数上绝对处于巨大的劣势。

sentences.en: So he says their numbers was the numbers of the French was so great as not to be even comparable with ours.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，法国人的数量大到甚至无法与我们相比。

sentences.en: And of course, he and Henry and everybody in the force is aware that there are other reasons why the English are not in peak fighting form,
sentences.zh: 当然，他和亨利以及军队中的所有人都意识到，英国人不在最佳战斗状态还有其他原因，

sentences.en: because they have travelled 250 miles in 17 days from Harfleur to the Somme, down the length of the Somme,
sentences.zh: 因为他们在17天里从哈勒弗勒到索姆河，沿着索姆河全长行军了250英里，

sentences.en: because the bridges and the fords and the causeways have been held against them, and then back up again.
sentences.zh: 因为桥梁、浅滩和堤道一直被敌人把守着，然后又折返回来。

sentences.en: And the corollary in turn of that is that they haven't eaten properly for several days, because Henry had only taken supplies for eight days.
sentences.zh: 与之相应的结果是，他们已经好几天没有吃好饭了，因为亨利只带了八天的补给。

sentences.en: The weather is terrible, kind of icy sleet.
sentences.zh: 天气糟糕透顶，下着冰冷的雨夹雪。

sentences.en: It's become very hilly, so they've been going up and down.
sentences.zh: 地势变得起伏不平，所以他们一直在上上下下。

sentences.en: So that's kind of more tiring than just marching across flat land.
sentences.zh: 这比单纯在平地上行军要劳累得多。

sentences.en: And I think it's clear when they see that force in front of them, they are feeling very demoralised.
sentences.zh: 我想很明显，当他们看到眼前的这支军队时，他们的士气非常低落。

sentences.en: The feeling that, you know, this is it.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就是，你知道的，这就是终点。

sentences.en: This is absolute curtains.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是大限已至。

sentences.en: But I do think that there is certainly one man in that army who does think, you know, we have a chance here.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，那支军队里肯定有一个人觉得，你知道的，我们这里还有机会。

sentences.en: And that man is Henry himself.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是亨利本人。

sentences.en: This is where individuals matter, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是个人发挥作用的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: The individuals do matter in war.
sentences.zh: 在战争中，个人确实很重要。

sentences.en: And this is why leadership and inspirational command really makes a difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么领导力和鼓舞人心的指挥真的能产生影响。

sentences.en: And it's why I think you can look at Shakespeare's play and say he burnishes Henry's reputation with this incredible poetry.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为你可以看看莎士比亚的戏剧，并说他用这些不可思议的诗句擦亮了亨利的声誉。

sentences.en: But I do think that Henry clearly deserves his reputation as an astonishing military commander with an ability to inspire people who otherwise might just have turned into a kind of despairing rabble.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，亨利显然无愧于他作为一位惊人的军事指挥官的声誉，他有能力鼓舞那些本来可能变成绝望暴民的人。

sentences.en: So everybody sees he feels no despair seeing the French army.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都看到，他在看到法军时并没有感到绝望。

sentences.en: So, again, the chaplain describes Henry observing the French very calmly and quite heedless of danger.
sentences.zh: 因此，牧师再次描述了亨利非常冷静地观察法军，完全不把危险放在眼里。

sentences.en: He orders his men to dismount, to ready themselves for battle.
sentences.zh: 他命令部下下马，为战斗做好准备。

sentences.en: Remember, he's ordered them to wear their armour, to wear their surcoats, to indicate the fact that they are ready for battle no matter when it happens.
sentences.zh: 记住，他命令他们穿上盔甲，穿上战袍，以表明无论何时发生战斗他们都已准备就绪。

sentences.en: He clearly stays on horseback.
sentences.zh: 他显然留在了马背上。

sentences.en: He rides along the battlefront.
sentences.zh: 他沿着战线骑马巡视。

sentences.en: He gives his stirring speech.
sentences.zh: 他发表了鼓舞人心的演讲。

sentences.en: So he tells them that they should have a fair day and a gracious victory in the better of their enemies.
sentences.zh: 因此他告诉他们，在战胜敌人之后，他们应该迎来美好的一天和荣耀的胜利。

sentences.en: He states bluntly, I am not going to be captured.
sentences.zh: 他直言不讳地说道，我绝不会被俘。

sentences.en: You know, if there is a defeat, then I will die in the battle rather than impose the burden of a ransom on the English.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果战败，我宁愿战死沙场，也不愿给英格兰强加赎金的负担。

sentences.en: And it's at this point, not as in Shakespeare, on the eve of the battle, that he makes his comment about not wanting any more men.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，而不是像莎士比亚那样在战前夕，他发表了关于不想再要任何人的评论。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: This is very Theoden at the charge of the Rahirim before Minas Tirith or something, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常像是《米那斯提力斯之战》前夕里奥丹率领洛汗骑兵冲锋的场景，不是吗？

sentences.en: The spectacle of the king on his horse and his men lined up before him and him genuinely, you know, infusing them with a sense of mission and a sense of inevitability, I guess,
sentences.zh: 国王骑在马背上，士兵们在他面前列队，他真诚地向他们灌输一种使命感和一种不可避免的宿命感，我想，

sentences.en: is what he gives them.
sentences.zh: 这就是他给予他们的。

sentences.en: I think absolutely that sense of he's clearly a very inspirational speaker.
sentences.zh: 我认为绝对有那种感觉，他显然是一个非常具有鼓舞力的演讲者。

sentences.en: But the difference is that he doesn't then launch a great charge because he assumes that they are going to be facing battle that day.
sentences.zh: 但不同的是，他并没有随即发起大规模冲锋，因为他认为他们当天就要面临战斗。

sentences.en: So he orders the priests to move through the lines, to take people's confessions.
sentences.zh: 所以他命令神职人员穿梭于各部队之间，倾听人们的忏悔。

sentences.en: And the English kneel down with their hands towards heaven.
sentences.zh: 英国士兵们双膝跪地，双手合十望向天堂。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are French accounts of the battle that they're impressed by this.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，法国对这场战役的记录中提到他们对此印象深刻。

sentences.en: So this has been a theme running throughout the march that Henry is kind of inspiring his men to share in his own sense of a divine purpose.
sentences.zh: 所以这是贯穿整个行军过程的一个主题，即亨利一直在鼓舞他的部下，让他们分享他对神圣使命的共同信念。

sentences.en: I think quite different to the, you know, the chevauché that the Black Prince or Edward III or Duke of Lancaster were launching in the first half.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与黑太子、爱德华三世或兰开斯特公爵在前半段发动的骑兵劫掠完全不同。

sentences.en: Henry is a very, very devout man.
sentences.zh: 亨利是一个非常非常虔诚的人。

sentences.en: And it's not a kind of hand-wringing, thought-for-the-day kind of Christianity.
sentences.zh: 这并不是那种唉声叹气、每日灵修式的基督教。

sentences.en: It's a martial, smite-them, God-is-on-our-side kind of Christianity.
sentences.zh: 这是一种崇尚武力、痛击敌人、上帝站在我们这一边的基督教。

sentences.en: And it clearly inspires the English.
sentences.zh: 这显然鼓舞了英国人。

sentences.en: So they are down kneeling, praying, you know, asking for God's blessing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们跪倒在地，祈祷，你知道的，祈求上帝的保佑。

sentences.en: But having done this, the French are not offering battle.
sentences.zh: 但做完这些后，法军并没有主动发起进攻。

sentences.en: No sign of movement at all from the army in front of them.
sentences.zh: 他们眼前的军队没有任何行动的迹象。

sentences.en: Henry keeps the English in battle formation.
sentences.zh: 亨利让英军保持战斗队形。

sentences.en: And when he sees the French starting to kind of move, people drifting across, he shifts the line so that they are always facing the French ranks.
sentences.zh: 当他看到法军开始有所行动、有人四处游荡时，他调整了战线，使他们始终面对法军的队列。

sentences.en: But dusk is closing in.
sentences.zh: 但暮色正在逼近。

sentences.en: You know, it's cold, it's wet, it's getting dark.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，天气寒冷，潮湿，天黑了。

sentences.en: And it becomes clear that, you know, there is going to be no battle that day.
sentences.zh: 很明显，你知道的，那天不会有任何战斗了。

sentences.en: The English can see the French kind of retiring to the nearby villages.
sentences.zh: 英国人可以看到法国人正在撤退到附近的村庄。

sentences.en: So Agincourt is one of them.
sentences.zh: 所以阿金库尔是其中之一。

sentences.en: Ruisseauville is another.
sentences.zh: 吕索维尔是另一个。

sentences.en: They're kind of settling down there.
sentences.zh: 他们在那儿安顿下来。

sentences.en: They're setting up their tents.
sentences.zh: 他们正在搭建帐篷。

sentences.en: Of course, I mean, that's agony for the English because they know that the French are going to be much better sheltered, much better fed.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，这对英国人来说是痛苦的，因为他们知道法国人将得到更好的庇护，得到更好的食物。

sentences.en: They're going to be regularly supplied.
sentences.zh: 他们将获得源源不断的补给。

sentences.en: But the English stay in battle order until it's completely dark and they can no longer see the enemy.
sentences.zh: 但英国人一直保持着战斗队形，直到天完全黑下来，再也看不到敌人为止。

sentences.en: And it's only at dusk, which is about 4.40, that Henry finally stands his army down.
sentences.zh: 直到大约四点四十的黄昏时刻，亨利才最终让他的军队原地休息。

sentences.en: The French have no urgency, right?
sentences.zh: 法国人不急，对吧？

sentences.en: Time is on their side.
sentences.zh: 时间站在他们这边。

sentences.en: They will accumulate more men probably as time goes on.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们可能会聚集更多的人。

sentences.en: And the English will become only more hungry, more tired, more wet, more miserable.
sentences.zh: 而英国人只会变得更饿、更累、更湿漉漉、更痛苦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So actually, I mean, it's the French interest to delay as long as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，拖延越久对法国人越有利。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And also more people will come in and join the French army because people are coming in from across northern France.
sentences.zh: 而且会有更多的人加入法国军队，因为人们正从法国北部各地赶来。

sentences.en: But Henry is still on high alert.
sentences.zh: 但亨利仍然高度警惕。

sentences.en: They are so close that they can see the French bonfires.
sentences.zh: 他们靠得太近了，甚至能看到法军的篝火。

sentences.en: They can hear them kind of chatting and talking.
sentences.zh: 他们能听到他们在闲聊和说话。

sentences.en: And again,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，

sentences.en: it's one of the themes that is brilliantly used by Shakespeare and derives from authentic memories of the battle that rumours spread through the English ranks that the French are dicing over the prisoners that they're going to take the following day.
sentences.zh: 这是莎士比亚巧妙运用并源自对战役真实记忆的主题之一，谣言在英国军队中传开，称法国人正在掷骰子决定第二天要俘虏的囚犯。

sentences.en: That they are so confident of victory that they're already working out who's going to get what prisoner.
sentences.zh: 他们对胜利如此自信，以至于已经在计算谁将分得哪个囚犯。

sentences.en: Arrogance.
sentences.zh: 傲慢。

sentences.en: Hubris, Tom.
sentences.zh: 狂妄，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: And so it's loud.
sentences.zh: 声音很大。

sentences.en: It's mouthy.
sentences.zh: 很吵闹。

sentences.en: It's boastful.
sentences.zh: 很自大。

sentences.en: The contrast, again, with the English ranks Henry has imposed, says, I don't want to hear a word.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，亨利对英军下达了禁令，说我不想听到任何声音。

sentences.en: No one is to talk.
sentences.zh: 任何人都不准说话。

sentences.en: So all that stuff you get in Shakespeare of Henry kind of wandering around and people chatting and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以你在莎士比亚作品中看到的那些亨利四处闲逛、大家聊天之类的场景。

sentences.en: This doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 这并没有发生。

sentences.en: There is total silence.
sentences.zh: 现场一片死寂。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is he wants to make it impossible for the French to launch a surprise attack by night.
sentences.zh: 原因是他想让法军无法在夜间发动突然袭击。

sentences.en: And of course, it's quite intimidating for the French.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对手法军来说相当具有威慑力。

sentences.en: They wonder, have the English slipped away?
sentences.zh: 他们在想，英国人是不是溜走了？

sentences.en: What is the meaning of this terrifying ominous silence?
sentences.zh: 这种可怕而不祥的沉默究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: So the rain is bucketing down.
sentences.zh: 雨下得倾盆而下。

sentences.en: The English soldiers try and find, you know, there are woods that they can shelter under the trees.
sentences.zh: 英国士兵试图寻找，你知道的，有一些树林他们可以在树下避难。

sentences.en: There are kind of hedges or whatever.
sentences.zh: 有一些树篱之类的东西。

sentences.en: They try and get what shelter they can.
sentences.zh: 他们设法寻找任何可以避难的地方。

sentences.en: Henry himself and his high command withdraw to a village in their rear called Maisonceles.
sentences.zh: 亨利本人和他的高级指挥官撤退到了他们后方的一个名为迈松塞勒的村庄。

sentences.en: They don't sleep there because they have a battle to plan.
sentences.zh: 他们没有在那里睡觉，因为他们还有一场战役要筹划。

sentences.en: And around midnight, Henry sends a group of pick knights to go out and to scout out the battlefield to work out the precise coordinates of the French lines.
sentences.zh: 午夜左右，亨利派出一队精锐骑士出去侦察战场，摸清法军阵地的精确坐标。

sentences.en: And when those knights come back and they deliver their report, then he and his high command finalize their battle plan.
sentences.zh: 当这些骑士回来并汇报情况后，他和他的高级指挥官们最终敲定了作战计划。

sentences.en: Henry does not sleep.
sentences.zh: 亨利没有睡觉。

sentences.en: His peers don't sleep.
sentences.zh: 他的部下们也没有睡觉。

sentences.en: Instead, he is armored and then fully armed.
sentences.zh: 相反，他先穿上重甲，然后武装齐备。

sentences.en: He hears three masses.
sentences.zh: 他听了三台弥撒。

sentences.en: So again, the sense that he's trusting in God.
sentences.zh: 所以再次体现出，他心中对上帝充满信任。

sentences.en: And then at dawn, as the sun rises, he puts on his helmet and his helmet has this crown kind of placed on the top.
sentences.zh: 然后在黎明时分，当太阳升起时，他戴上了头盔，头盔顶部有一个王冠似的东西。

sentences.en: And the crown has the emblems of both England and France, bright gold.
sentences.zh: 王冠上有英格兰和法兰克王国的徽章，金光闪闪。

sentences.en: And this means that there will be no missing him in battle.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他在战斗中绝不会被人忽视。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So all those Frenchmen who are looking to capture the king, they know exactly where he is.
sentences.zh: 所以所有那些想要俘虏国王的法国人，都能确切知道他在哪里。

sentences.en: And as we will see, this is very deliberate.
sentences.zh: 正如我们接下来将看到的，这是非常蓄意安排的。

sentences.en: Henry's not a man who would employ doubles, right?
sentences.zh: 亨利不是那种会雇用替身的人，对吧？

sentences.en: No, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对不是。

sentences.en: And then in preparation for ordering his battle ranks, he doesn't climb onto a charger.
sentences.zh: 接着，在准备排兵布阵时，他没有骑上战马。

sentences.en: He climbs onto a small gray horse.
sentences.zh: 他骑上了一匹灰色的瘦小马驹。

sentences.en: And I think this is so emblematic of his character.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常能代表他的性格。

sentences.en: On the one hand, incredible degree of self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 一方面，他有着惊人的自信。

sentences.en: But at the same time, also this kind of Christian sense of humility fused into this idea of him on a small gray horse.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，骑在小灰马上的这种形象中，也融进了一种基督教式的谦逊之感。

sentences.en: He's drawing attention to the fact that he is humble as well as confident.
sentences.zh: 他在向外界传达这样一个事实：他既谦逊又自信。

sentences.en: And riding on the horse, he orders his men to take up their positions.
sentences.zh: 他骑在马上，命令手下各就各位。

sentences.en: So what is his plan?
sentences.zh: 那么他的计划是什么？

sentences.en: What is this strategy that he and his peers have been devising through the night?
sentences.zh: 他和部下们整夜在筹划的这个战略究竟是什么？

sentences.en: It's determined by two factors.
sentences.zh: 它由两个因素决定。

sentences.en: And the first of these is the terrain.
sentences.zh: 其中第一个是地形。

sentences.en: And the second is the makeup of his army.
sentences.zh: 第二个是他军队的组成结构。

sentences.en: And both of them are quite distinctive.
sentences.zh: 这两者都相当独特。

sentences.en: So the terrain firSt.
sentences.zh: 先说地形。

sentences.en: They are on the road to Calais.
sentences.zh: 他们正走在去加来（Calais）的路上。

sentences.en: The French have blocked them.
sentences.zh: 法国人挡住了他们的去路。

sentences.en: And this road, the reason the French have blocked them where they are is that there's expansive, relatively flat fields.
sentences.zh: 这条路之所以被法国人选在此处拦截，是因为这里有广阔且相对平坦的田野。

sentences.en: There is a slight dip.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个微小的凹陷。

sentences.en: So between the French and the English, there's a slight declivity, which means that whoever is going to be attacking will have to kind of go down and then up.
sentences.zh: 所以在法军和英军之间，有一个轻微的倾斜坡度，这意味着任何一方要发起进攻，都必须先下坡再上坡。

sentences.en: It's not steep, but it's a mild kind of gradient.
sentences.zh: 它不是很陡，而是一个缓坡。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The fields have recently been ploughed.
sentences.zh: 这些田地最近刚被犁过。

sentences.en: The soil here, it's not kind of light.
sentences.zh: 这里的土壤并不松轻。

sentences.en: It's not the kind of soil where rain would drain away easily.
sentences.zh: 它不是那种雨水能轻易渗走的土壤。

sentences.en: It's thick, heavy clay.
sentences.zh: 那是厚重黏稠的粘土。

sentences.en: And that means that the ground is pretty sodden.
sentences.zh: 这意味着地面相当湿润泥泞。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that is something else that Henry is factoring into his plans for the battle.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是亨利在制定作战计划时考虑到的因素之一。

sentences.en: I mean, anyone who's read the Lady Bird book or something knows that Agincourt is a very muddy battle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何读过《Lady Bird》儿童读物或其他类似书籍的人都知道，阿金库尔是一场非常泥泞的战役。

sentences.en: Well, yes, I remember one of the first books I read on Agincourt was John Keegan's Face of Battle, which is about Agincourt, Waterloo and the Somme.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我记得我读过的关于阿金库尔的第一本书之一是约翰·基根（John Keegan）的《战争的面貌》（Face of Battle），这本书讲的是阿金库尔、滑铁卢和索姆河战役。

sentences.en: And Agincourt and the Somme both have mud.
sentences.zh: 阿金库尔和索姆河都有泥泞。

sentences.en: They do indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: As a kind of a biting theme.
sentences.zh: 作为一个贯穿始终的主题。

sentences.en: So there's this road, there's ploughed fields, potentially very muddy.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有路，有耕地，而且可能非常泥泞。

sentences.en: There are two villages on either side of the road and they're about a kilometre apart.
sentences.zh: 路的两侧各有两个村庄，相距约一公里。

sentences.en: So there's Agincourt on the left of the English as they're facing the French.
sentences.zh: 当英军面向法军时，阿金库尔村在英军的左侧。

sentences.en: And there's a village called Tramacourt on the right.
sentences.zh: 右侧则是一个叫特拉马库尔（Tramacourt）的村庄。

sentences.en: The battlefield is also bounded by woodland on both sides.
sentences.zh: 战场两侧还被树林所环绕。

sentences.en: And this woodland tapers in from the French positions.
sentences.zh: 从法军阵地开始，这些树林向内收窄。

sentences.en: I mean, again, not massively, but to a significant degree towards the English positions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，同样，收窄幅度虽不算巨大，但朝着英军阵地方向来看，程度相当显著。

sentences.en: So this is good for the English because, of course, they have far fewer men at arMs.
sentences.zh: 这对英军很有利，因为当然了，他们参战的人数要少得多。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll come to the precise numbers.
sentences.zh: 也许我们稍后会谈到确切的数字。

sentences.en: But I reckon around a thousand.
sentences.zh: 但我估计大约有一千人。

sentences.en: And the French have many, many multiples of that.
sentences.zh: 而法军的人数是这个数字的好几倍。

sentences.en: So the fact that they can't be outflanked because there are the woods is very important.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于有树林阻挡而不会被侧翼包抄，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: And it also means that if the French advance towards the English, the ground in front of them will narrow.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着，如果法军向英军推进，他们前方的地面将会变窄。

sentences.en: They will have to kind of crowd close and close together as they approach the English lines.
sentences.zh: 当他们接近英军防线时，不得不越挤越紧。

sentences.en: Yes, it does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so this then segues with the composition of Henry's forces to determine how he's going to kind of line up his rank.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就与亨利军队的构成结合起来，决定了他将如何排兵布阵。

sentences.en: So it's conventional in battles in this period for armies to basically divide it into three positions.
sentences.zh: 当时那个时期的战役中，军队通常基本上分为三个阵地。

sentences.en: And Henry does this again.
sentences.zh: 亨利也沿用了这种做法。

sentences.en: Normally, you'd have a front rank, you'd have a vanguard, you'd have a main body, and then you'd have a rear guard.
sentences.zh: 通常，你会有一个前锋阵营，一个先锋队，一个主力部队，然后还有一个后卫部队。

sentences.en: Henry can't afford to do that.
sentences.zh: 亨利无力做到这一点。

sentences.en: He doesn't have enough men to do that.
sentences.zh: 他没有足够的人手来那样做。

sentences.en: So instead, he draws them in a kind of line across this kilometer of open field between the woods on either side.
sentences.zh: 所以相反，他在两侧树林之间一公里宽的开阔地上，把他们排成了一条横线。

sentences.en: And the result is a kind of, I suppose, a thin silver line, you might call it.
sentences.zh: 结果就是一种——我想你可以称之为一条银色的细线。

sentences.en: I was about to say, a thin red line.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，一条火红的细线。

sentences.en: So Henry commands the central division.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利指挥中央部队。

sentences.en: And remember, he's got this gold crown.
sentences.zh: 记住，他戴着这个金王冠。

sentences.en: He's got his banner.
sentences.zh: 他带着他的军旗。

sentences.en: There's no way the French are going to be able to miss him.
sentences.zh: 法国人绝不可能认不出他。

sentences.en: He is in the middle of the middle division.
sentences.zh: 他就身处中央部队的正中间。

sentences.en: On his right, he has a division commanded by the Duke of York, who is close cousin of Henry's.
sentences.zh: 在他的右侧，是约克公爵（Duke of York）指挥的部队，他是亨利的近亲。

sentences.en: He's a great fan of Chaucer, and perhaps not coincidentally, that being so, he's written a great, famous treatise on hunting in English.
sentences.zh: 他是乔叟（Chaucer）的超级粉丝，也许并非巧合的是，正因如此，他用英文写了一篇非常著名、关于狩猎的专著。

sentences.en: So he's properly an English peer.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个根正苗红的英国贵族。

sentences.en: And to Henry's left is the third division, which is commanded by a guy called Thomas Lord
sentences.zh: 而在亨利的左侧是第三支部队，由一个叫托马斯·洛德

sentences.en: Camois.
sentences.zh: 卡莫瓦（Thomas Lord Camoys）的人指挥。

sentences.en: And the reason that he's put in command is that he is 65.
sentences.zh: 之所以让他担任指挥，是因为他已经65岁了。

sentences.en: So he brings many, many years of experience.
sentences.zh: 因此他带来了丰富的经验。

sentences.en: All three divisions consist of men at arMs.
sentences.zh: 这三个部队都由重甲骑兵（步行骑士）组成。

sentences.en: So none of the English, not even the king, is going to be on horseback.
sentences.zh: 所以所有英国人，甚至连国王在内，都不会骑马作战。

sentences.en: But of course, the key decision for Henry is where he's going to place the main body of his army, which consists of archers.
sentences.zh: 但对亨利来说，最关键的决定当然是把由弓箭手组成的主力部队部署在哪里。

sentences.en: And the precise details of this is much debated.
sentences.zh: 关于这方面的具体细节有很多争论。

sentences.en: I mean, you can read multiple accounts of Agincourt, and they all have slightly different sense of where it is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以读到多份关于阿金库尔战役的记载，它们对部署位置的说法都略有不同。

sentences.en: But I think the outline is pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 但我认为总体轮廓相当清晰。

sentences.en: Henry places large blocks of archers on both wings, kind of sheltered by trees in the woods, some of them.
sentences.zh: 亨利在两翼部署了大量弓箭手，其中一些受到树林中树木的掩护。

sentences.en: And he also positions them in wedges between the three divisions.
sentences.zh: 他还把他们呈楔形部署在三个部队之间。

sentences.en: So in two wedges.
sentences.zh: 也就是形成两个楔形阵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And these are placed under another man who is very distinguished and really quite elderly.
sentences.zh: 这些部队交由另一位身份显赫且年事已高的人物指挥。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Sir Thomas Irpingham, who is the most loyal of loyalist Lancastrians.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是托马斯·厄平汉爵士（Sir Thomas Erpingham），他是兰开斯特派中最忠诚的忠臣。

sentences.en: His loyalty to Lancaster goes back to Henry IV before Henry became king.
sentences.zh: 他对兰开斯特家族的忠诚可以追溯到亨利四世登基之前。

sentences.en: Thomas Irpingham had accompanied him on, you know, crusade where Henry picked up his ostrich and gone to Jerusalem and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·厄平汉曾陪同他去过十字军东征（你知道的，亨利在那里摘取了鸵鸟羽毛饰物，去过耶路撒冷以及诸如此类的事情）。

sentences.en: So Irpingham really is, I mean, properly seasoned.
sentences.zh: 所以厄平汉可以说是经历极其丰富、身经百战。

sentences.en: Oh, very much so.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实如此。

sentences.en: And completely reliable.
sentences.zh: 而且绝对可靠。

sentences.en: So he was again with Henry in exile.
sentences.zh: 因此，他曾再次陪同亨利流亡。

sentences.en: He accompanies Henry back to England when he overthrows Richard II.
sentences.zh: 当亨利推翻理查二世时，他陪伴亨利回到了英格兰。

sentences.en: So he's been there.
sentences.zh: 所以他一直在场。

sentences.en: He's seen everything.
sentences.zh: 他见证了一切。

sentences.en: And the fact that he's now in command of the archers reflects the fact that Henry is putting a premium on experience.
sentences.zh: 他现在负责指挥弓箭手，这反映出亨利将经验放在首位。

sentences.en: He wants people who he can absolutely rely on to hold his back and to do the right thing, even in conditions of incredible tension and danger.
sentences.zh: 他需要那些绝对可以信赖、能为他守住后方并在哪怕极度紧张和危险的情况下也能做对事情的人。

sentences.en: But at the same time as Henry is emphasising experience, he's also not afraid to innovate.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，在强调经验的同时，亨利也并不害怕创新。

sentences.en: And so this is why on the march, he had ordered his archers, even though they were weary, tired,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在行军途中，他曾命令他的弓箭手们，尽管他们已经精疲力竭、疲惫不堪、

sentences.en: hungry, to make themselves some wooden stakes, sharp stakes, and to carry them as well with everything else.
sentences.zh: 饥肠辘辘，也要削制一些木桩、尖木桩，并在携带其他所有装备的同时把它们带上。

sentences.en: And this is something that Edward III's armies, for instance, had not had.
sentences.zh: 这是英王爱德华三世（Edward III）的军队所没有的东西。

sentences.en: It's something that is quite novel.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当新颖的做法。

sentences.en: And so there are various kind of debates as to where Henry might have got the idea from it.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于亨利这个灵感从何而来，存在各种各样的争论。

sentences.en: And one thesis is that the Turks had used stakes like this with their archers against the knights
sentences.zh: 其中一种观点认为，土耳其人曾在尼科波利斯（Nicopolis）之战中

sentences.en: at Nicopolis, the great disaster for Christian arms in 1396 that Marshal Busco had fought in, the great French paladin.
sentences.zh: 对阵骑士时使用过这种带弓箭手的木桩。那是1396年基督教军队的一场大灾难，伟大的法国游侠布西科（Marshal Boucicaut）曾参战。

sentences.en: I think a likelier theory is that Henry is remembering the Battle of Shrewsbury.
sentences.zh: 我认为更合理的理论是亨利记起了什鲁斯伯里战役（Battle of Shrewsbury）。

sentences.en: Right, because that was the pea field.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为那是豌豆田之战。

sentences.en: The pea field with the stakes.
sentences.zh: 长满豌豆、插着木桩的田地。

sentences.en: Stakes there, right?
sentences.zh: 那里的木桩，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And of course, that was the battle where he'd been hit in the face by the arrow.
sentences.zh: 当然，那也是他曾被箭射中面部的战役。

sentences.en: So a very traumatic and defining experience for him.
sentences.zh: 所以对他来说这是一段非常痛苦且具有决定意义的经历。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that he would remember that.
sentences.zh: 因此他会记住这一点是在情理之中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's, I think, important to emphasize that battles are rare events.
sentences.zh: 我认为值得强调的是，会战是罕见的事件。

sentences.en: Pitched battles are rare events.
sentences.zh: 阵地会战是罕见的事件。

sentences.en: They don't come along very often.
sentences.zh: 它们不会经常发生。

sentences.en: But Henry had experienced one when he was very, very young.
sentences.zh: 但亨利在非常非常年轻的时候就经历过一次。

sentences.en: And I think the memory of the role that these stakes had played, which of course weren't sharp because they were used for holding up peas, but they had prevented a mass charge by
sentences.zh: 我认为这些木桩所起作用的记忆——当然它们以前并不是尖的，因为它们是用来支撑豌豆藤的，但它们曾阻止了

sentences.en: his father's men.
sentences.zh: 他父亲手下军队的大规模冲锋。

sentences.en: I'm sure that probably this is where he gets the idea for it.
sentences.zh: 我确信这大概就是他获得灵感的地方。

sentences.en: And of course, the broader experience, as you said, that Henry had from Shrewsbury is being hit in the face by an arrow.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如你所说，亨利从什鲁斯伯里获得的更广泛的经历就是被箭射中面部。

sentences.en: So he knows what the impact is.
sentences.zh: 所以他知道那种冲击力是怎样的。

sentences.en: I mean, he knows how devastating, you know, a hail storm of arrows can be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他知道箭如雨下会有多么毁灭性的杀伤力。

sentences.en: And that's why I think it's based on the memories of that.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为这是基于当时的记忆。

sentences.en: You know, maybe he doesn't expect to win, but he feels he's in with a very, very good chance.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许他并没有期望获胜，但他觉得自已获胜的机会非常非常大。

sentences.en: But of course, he's not the only one with a plan.
sentences.zh: 当然，拥有计划的不止他一个人。

sentences.en: The French have a battle plan as well.
sentences.zh: 法军也有作战计划。

sentences.en: And we know this because we actually have it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点，因为我们实际拥有它。

sentences.en: It's one of only a couple of battle plans to have survived from this period.
sentences.zh: 这是从那个时期流传下来的仅有的几份作战计划之一。

sentences.en: This is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's incredible.
sentences.zh: 是的，难以置信。

sentences.en: So they put it down on paper or on parchment or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把它写在纸上或羊皮纸上或者其他什么东西上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They'd drawn it up a few days before.
sentences.zh: 他们在几天前就拟定好了。

sentences.en: And it had been drawn up by the two great professional soldiers in the French ranks.
sentences.zh: 这份计划是由法军阵营中两位伟大的职业军人拟定的。

sentences.en: So Boussicot, who we've mentioned, the great paladin, and Dalbray, who is the constable, the guy who kind of has a nominal control.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们提到过的伟大游侠布西科（Boucicaut），以及担任统帅、名义上拥有控制权的阿尔布雷特（Dalbray）。

sentences.en: But there are two problems with it.
sentences.zh: 但它有两个问题。

sentences.en: The first is that they'd actually drawn it up several days before.
sentences.zh: 首先是他们实际上在几天前就拟定好了。

sentences.en: And it doesn't exactly correspond to the terrain that you get at Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 它与你在阿金库尔实际见到的地形并不完全吻合。

sentences.en: But the other problem is that they are no longer really in control.
sentences.zh: 但另一个问题是，他们实际上已经失去了控制。

sentences.en: Their command has been superseded by the fact that large quantities of very high ranking peers have turned up.
sentences.zh: 由于大量身份极高的贵族涌现，他们的指挥权已经被取代了。

sentences.en: So their original plan was to divide the army into two, that the front rank would be commanded by Boussicot and Dalbray as the professional soldiers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最初的计划是将军队分为两部分，前锋由职业军人布西科和达布雷指挥。

sentences.en: Because they knew that they would be marching into the English arrow storm.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道自己将迎着英军的箭雨行军。

sentences.en: And Dalbray in particular, he has fought the English.
sentences.zh: 尤其是达布雷，他跟英国人打过仗。

sentences.en: I mean, he's that old that he'd been part of the war back in Edward III's time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他年纪很大了，甚至参加过爱德华三世时期的战争。

sentences.en: And it's a slight myth, isn't it, that they take the English lightly?
sentences.zh: 他们轻视英国人，这其实是个小小的误区，对吧？

sentences.en: Because these guys, they know that the English, they remember the battles in the first bit of the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 因为这些人很清楚英国人，他们还记得百年战争早期的那些战役。

sentences.en: They know that Henry V, he knows what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 他们知道亨利五世很清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: They are not underestimating him.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有低估他。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in fact, they didn't really want to battle at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们其实根本不想打这一仗。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think they would have been perfectly happy not to fight a battle at all and just let Henry's army disintegrate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得他们完全乐意不打这一仗，就让亨利的军队自己瓦解。

sentences.en: They'd have been fine with that.
sentences.zh: 他们完全能接受这一点。

sentences.en: They've been told basically by the king, by the Dauphin, by the peers of the realm, no, we have to fight.
sentences.zh: 国王、王太子和王国贵族基本上都告诉他们：不，我们必须迎战。

sentences.en: And so they've drawn up this plan where Boussicot and Dalbray will command the vanguard.
sentences.zh: 于是他们拟定了这个计划，由布西科和达布雷指挥先锋。

sentences.en: And then the second, the main body will be commanded by the Duke of Alassan, who's this great kind of boar of a man.
sentences.zh: 然后第二部分，即主力部队，将由阿朗松公爵指挥，他是个身材魁梧、像野猪一样的猛将。

sentences.en: They'll put crossbow men on the wings and they will have an elite force of cavalry that will be used to clear the archers.
sentences.zh: 他们会把弩手部署在两翼，并拥有一支精锐骑兵部队，用来消灭敌方的弓箭手。

sentences.en: And it will be kind of total warfare, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场全方位的战争，多米尼克。

sentences.en: So the crossbow men will fire, the men at arms will charge, the cavalry will sweep down on the archers and get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 所以弩手会开火，重骑兵会冲锋，骑兵会席卷弓箭手并消灭他们。

sentences.en: And, you know, the English basically won't know what's hit them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，英国人基本上根本不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: They'll be overwhelmed in a single devastating moment of impact.
sentences.zh: 他们会在一个毁灭性的瞬间被彻底压垮。

sentences.en: It's kind of Nelsonian, go straight at them and use our firepower to blast them out of the way.
sentences.zh: 这有点像纳尔逊式的战术，直接冲向敌人，用火力把他们轰开。

sentences.en: Just everything, throw everything you've got at them.
sentences.zh: 把一切都押上，把你能用的一切都砸向他们。

sentences.en: But the problem is because of the woods, the cavalry is not in a position to march down and sweep the archers away.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，由于树林的阻挡，骑兵无法冲过去消灭弓箭手。

sentences.en: So they can't outflank them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们无法从侧翼包抄。

sentences.en: So that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这就成了一个问题。

sentences.en: But the other problem is, is that because all these dukes and counts, you know, members of the royal family have arrived, they outrank Boussicot and Dalbray.
sentences.zh: 但另一个问题是，由于所有这些公爵、伯爵，也就是王室成员都到了，他们的军衔比布西科和达布雷还要高。

sentences.en: And because the king isn't there, because the Dauphin isn't there, because the Duke of
sentences.zh: 而且因为国王不在，王太子不在，因为...

sentences.en: Orléans, who is the highest ranking royal member of the family, is there, but he's quite young.
sentences.zh: 作为王室最高成员的奥尔良公爵在场，但他相当年轻。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, you know, his birthday is in a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他的生日就在几天后。

sentences.en: There isn't actually now an obvious commander.
sentences.zh: 所以现在其实没有一个明显的主帅。

sentences.en: They're all kind of shouting and yelling and claiming precedence.
sentences.zh: 大家都在那里大喊大叫，争夺资历和地位。

sentences.en: They spend all night kind of basically arguing about where they should all go because you've got all these dukes, all these counts.
sentences.zh: 他们花了一整夜的时间争论每个人该站在哪里，因为有这么多的公爵和伯爵。

sentences.en: They're not going to hang around at the rear.
sentences.zh: 他们可不打算待在后方。

sentences.en: They want to be in the front.
sentences.zh: 他们都想冲在最前面。

sentences.en: So finally, they come to a conclusion.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，他们达成了一个结论。

sentences.en: I quote Juliet Barker in her wonderful book on Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 我引用朱丽叶·巴克在她那本关于阿金库尔的出色著作中的话。

sentences.en: She says it's a conclusion that was fair, but foolish.
sentences.zh: 她说这是一个公平但愚蠢的结论。

sentences.en: And basically, the solution is that they will all fight in the front line, although Alonso will retain his command of the main body of the army behind them.
sentences.zh: 基本上，解决办法是他们将全部在最前线作战，尽管阿朗松仍将保留对他们身后主力部队的指挥权。

sentences.en: And this means that they have to lengthen the line to fit in all these peers and dukes and things, which in turn means that there is no room for the archers and the crossbowmen.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们必须拉长战线，才能容纳下所有这些贵族和公爵，而这反过来又意味着根本没有空间留给弓箭手和弩手了。

sentences.en: So the solution to this is, oh, we'll just get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 所以解决办法就是：哦，干脆把他们弄走算了。

sentences.en: We'll put them at the back of the army.
sentences.zh: 把他们安排在军队最后方。

sentences.en: That's bonkers.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: That's bonkers.
sentences.zh: 这简直荒谬。

sentences.en: So just before we go to the break, Tom, I know this is very controversial among historians.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们休息一下之前，汤姆，我知道这在历史学家中非常有争议。

sentences.en: Talk us through the numbers because for those of us who grew up in England reading kind of old-fashioned patriotic history books, the impression we were given was that, you
sentences.zh: 跟我们聊聊人数吧，因为对于我们这些在英格兰读着老派爱国历史书长大的人来说，我们得到的印象是...

sentences.en: know, for every hundred Frenchmen, there was one Englishman or something like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大约每有一百个法国人，就只有一个英国人诸如此类的。

sentences.en: But it is true, isn't it, that whatever historians think about the numbers, there are very, very different accounts.
sentences.zh: 但不管历史学家对人数有何看法，确实存在非常、非常不同的记载，对吧？

sentences.en: There is no doubt there are far more Frenchmen than there are Englishmen.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，法国人远多于英国人。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, so this has always basically been taken for granted and not just by English historians, by French historians as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这一点基本上一直是理所当然的，不仅英国历史学家这么认为，法国历史学家也是如此。

sentences.en: It's not just, you know, patriotic chauvinism that leads people to say that.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是那种让人说出这种话的爱国沙文主义。

sentences.en: The overwhelming body of the sources emphasised the fact that the English were very, very outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数史料都强调这样一个事实：英国人在数量上处于极其劣势。

sentences.en: And it seems to me clear that, you know, we said this at the beginning of the show, that
sentences.zh: 在我看来很清楚的是，我们在节目一开始就说过...

sentences.en: the reason why it has this resonance is because from the beginning, the English believe this.
sentences.zh: 它之所以能产生共鸣，是因为从一开始，英国人自己就是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And to reiterate that, I would say the conventional estimate on the numbers of the English stage and corps is around 6,000 men.
sentences.zh: 为了重申这一点，我想说，对英军总人数的常规估计大约是6000人。

sentences.en: So 1,000 men at arms, about 5,000 archers.
sentences.zh: 其中1000名重骑兵，大约5000名弓箭手。

sentences.en: And this is based on the evidence of the two eyewitnesses at the battle who were on the
sentences.zh: 这基于亲历战役的两名英国阵营目击者的证据。

sentences.en: English side.
sentences.zh: 英国人。

sentences.en: So the chaplain who we've mentioned, and there's also a Burgundian lord who was fighting with the English called Jean Lefebvre, and their estimates kind of, they balance out.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们提到过的那个随军牧师，还有一个与英格兰并肩作战的勃艮第领主叫让·勒费弗尔，他们的估计基本上是不相上下。

sentences.en: But the reason why these figures have become controversial over the past 20 years is because
sentences.zh: 但这些数字在过去20年里变得颇具争议的原因是...

sentences.en: Anne Currie, the great historian of the Agincourt campaign.
sentences.zh: 安妮·柯里，阿金库尔战役的伟大历史学家。

sentences.en: And herald.
sentences.zh: 还有纹章官。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she wrote this kind of game-changing book called Agincourt, A New History.
sentences.zh: 所以她写了一本颠覆性的书，叫做《阿金库尔：一部新历史》。

sentences.en: It came out in 2005, and then it was reissued in 2015 for the anniversary of the battle.
sentences.zh: 它于2005年出版，后来在2015年战役周年纪念时再版。

sentences.en: And she had gone through loads of primary sources.
sentences.zh: 她翻阅了大量的原始史料。

sentences.en: She'd looked at all the scrolls that no one had looked at since 1415 and so on.
sentences.zh: 她查看了所有自1415年以来就无人问津的卷轴等等。

sentences.en: And she crunched the numbers.
sentences.zh: 并且她仔细核算过这些数字。

sentences.en: And she'd particularly focused on the recruitment and the composition of the various English contingents that went on the Agincourt campaign.
sentences.zh: 她特别关注了参加阿金库尔战役的各支英国分遣队的招募情况和人员构成。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely indispensable work.
sentences.zh: 这是绝对不可或缺的著作。

sentences.en: I mean, I've shamelessly drawn on it for these episodes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在这些单集里也毫不脸红地借鉴了它。

sentences.en: But it is also, the controversy is that she uses these documents, these primary sources, to estimate that Henry's army had been maybe as high as 9,000.
sentences.zh: 但争议在于，她利用这些文件和原始史料估算，亨利的军队人数可能高达9000人。

sentences.en: Actually, over the course of her book, her estimate of how large Henry's numbers were rises and rises and rises.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在她的书的进程中，她对亨利军队规模的估计一直在不断攀升。

sentences.en: And her estimate of the numbers of the French is that they're around 12,000.
sentences.zh: 而她对法军人数的估计则在12000人左右。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that would be an imbalance of four to three.
sentences.zh: 所以比例大概是四比三的失衡。

sentences.en: So the French have a larger force, but it's not the kind of victory against overwhelming odds that tradition says it is.
sentences.zh: 因此法军拥有更庞大的军队，但这并不是传统所说的那种以寡敌众的辉煌胜利。

sentences.en: There has been, I think, quite a kind of kickback against that.
sentences.zh: 我认为，对此已经产生了不少强烈的反弹。

sentences.en: So Juliette Barker, in her book on Agincourt, I mean, she absolutely acknowledges, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以朱丽叶·巴克在她关于阿金库尔的书里，我的意思是，她完全承认...

sentences.en: there's no one who has a comparable knowledge of the minutiae of the financial administrative documents of the campaign.
sentences.zh: 没有人对战役的财政和行政文件细节有着如此无与伦比的了解。

sentences.en: Professor Currie is absolutely the leader on this.
sentences.zh: 柯里教授在这方面绝对是泰斗。

sentences.en: But she does kick back against it.
sentences.zh: 但她的确进行了回击。

sentences.en: And the reason that she does this is, firstly, looking at the French numbers.
sentences.zh: 她这样做的原因，首先是审视法国的人数。

sentences.en: Basically, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们并不清楚。

sentences.en: We don't have the documents that would enable us to work it out because of the wars of religion, the French Revolution, and so on.
sentences.zh: 由于宗教战争、法国大革命等等原因，我们没有能够计算出具体数字的文件。

sentences.en: They were lost, right?
sentences.zh: 它们都丢失了，对吧？

sentences.en: They're all destroyed.
sentences.zh: 全都毁了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They've all just been loSt.
sentences.zh: 它们就这样不见了。

sentences.en: We just can't know.
sentences.zh: 我们根本无从得知。

sentences.en: But the point she makes that does seem to me...
sentences.zh: 但她提出的这一点在我看来确实...

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe I want to believe it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许我想相信这一点。

sentences.en: I probably do want to believe it.
sentences.zh: 我可能确实想相信它。

sentences.en: But it does seem to me, really, the clinching argument is that all the sources from the beginning emphasize that the victory is won against overwhelming odds.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，真正具决定性的论据是，从一开始所有的史料都强调这场胜利是在极端悬殊的劣势下取得的。

sentences.en: And I think that if Anne Currie's figures are accurate, that doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果安妮·柯里的数字是准确的，那就说不通了。

sentences.en: And I think that when you look at her figures, I mean, I think she said before, she's very much not Team Henry.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为当你看看她的数字时，就像她以前说过的那样，她绝对不是“亨利战队”的人。

sentences.en: She doesn't seem to like Henry very much at all.
sentences.zh: 她看起来一点也不喜欢亨利。

sentences.en: She has a tendency to make the English figures as high as she can and the French figures as low as she can.
sentences.zh: 她有一种倾向，尽量把英国人的数字写得越高越好，而把法国人的数字写得越低越好。

sentences.en: So I'm sure, Dominic, you, maybe lots of our listeners, maybe not our French listeners, if we have any, but I think that they can listen to this and feel that the traditional
sentences.zh: 所以我确信，多米尼克，你，也许还有我们的许多听众——如果没有法国听众的话——在听了这些之后，会觉得英国人处于劣势的传统说法，大概是二比一吧，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: account of the English being outnumbered, probably two to one, I would think.
sentences.zh: 也许是二比一。

sentences.zh: 随后他下令全军向前推进。

sentences.en: Every English soldier kneels, kisses the ground, and they do this thing where they take a piece of soil and put it in their mouth.
sentences.zh: 每个英国士兵都跪下，亲吻土地，他们还抓起一把泥土放进嘴里。

sentences.en: And it's a kind of trusting themselves to God kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种将自己托付给上帝的仪式。

sentences.en: And they've done that.
sentences.zh: 他们做完了这些。

sentences.en: And then Henry gives the battle cry, St. George, this day, help thine own.
sentences.zh: 然后亨利发出战斗口号：“圣乔治，今日护佑你自己的子民！”

sentences.en: Massive cheer.
sentences.zh: 爆发出巨大的欢呼声。

sentences.en: And they start advancing.
sentences.zh: 他们开始前进。

sentences.en: But this is the moment of peril, because for the archers, who are maybe five sixths of the entire army, you know, they are basically defenseless at this point.
sentences.zh: 但这正是最危险的时刻，因为对于占全军五分之四多的弓箭手来说，你知道的，他们此刻基本上毫无防备。

sentences.en: They have to pull their stakes up, move forward, hammer the stakes back in.
sentences.zh: 他们必须拔起木桩，向前移动，再把木桩重新砸进地里。

sentences.en: And the whole time, if the French cavalry had charged, they would have been in no position to fire back.
sentences.zh: 而如果在这整个过程中法国骑兵发起冲锋，他们根本无法还击。

sentences.en: They would have just been overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 他们只会全军覆没。

sentences.en: So for Henry, this is, I mean, you can imagine it.
sentences.zh: 所以对亨利来说，你可以想象一下。

sentences.en: His heart must have been in his mouth.
sentences.zh: 他当时必定心急如焚。

sentences.en: Why don't the French charge?
sentences.zh: 为什么法国人不冲锋呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底怎么回事？

sentences.en: I think because they're taken by surprise.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为他们被打了个措手不及。

sentences.en: They can't believe that the English would have the nerve to advance on them.
sentences.zh: 他们简直不敢相信英国人竟然有胆量主动向他们进攻。

sentences.en: And so, you know, they're not on their horses.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他们当时没骑马。

sentences.en: They're not in the front line.
sentences.zh: 他们不在最前线。

sentences.en: They're not ready to go.
sentences.zh: 他们还没准备好战斗。

sentences.en: And this is an absolute disastrous failure on the French part, because the French line is now within the range of the English longbows.
sentences.zh: 这对法军来说是一个绝对灾难性的失误，因为英军的阵线已经进入了英国长弓的射程之内。

sentences.en: And Sir Thomas Irpingham, who is the, you know, the old veteran who's in charge of the
sentences.zh: 负责指挥弓箭手的老兵托马斯·厄平汉爵士，

sentences.en: archers, he's got this bat on and he throws it in the air as a signal that they should unleash their first volley.
sentences.zh: 他拿着一根指挥棒将其抛向空中，作为射出第一轮箭雨的信号。

sentences.en: And this is what they do.
sentences.zh: 他们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: So in the first minute, 75,000 arrows rain down on the French lines.
sentences.zh: 因此在第一分钟里，75000支箭如雨点般倾泻在法军阵地上。

sentences.en: And by this point, the French cavalry have got their act together and are charging.
sentences.zh: 而此时，法国骑兵终于反应过来并开始冲锋。

sentences.en: And they are charging into darkness because these arrows, you know, they blot out the sun and there's no need for the English to kill the knights.
sentences.zh: 他们是在一片黑暗中冲锋的，因为这些箭遮蔽了太阳，而且英国人根本不需要杀死骑士。

sentences.en: The developments in armour are so impressive that most of the arrows just kind of bounce off the plate.
sentences.zh: 盔甲的技术进步如此惊人，以至于大多数箭射到板甲上都直接弹开了。

sentences.en: But what they need to do is to knock the knights off their horses.
sentences.zh: 但他们需要做的是把骑士从马上撞下来。

sentences.en: And the sheer volume of arrows descending in this kind of storm is more than sufficient to do that.
sentences.zh: 这种如暴雨般倾泻而下的庞大箭量，足以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Or, of course, to bring the horses down.
sentences.zh: 或者，当然，也可以把战马射翻在地。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: 75,000 arrows.
I mean, you can't imagine it, can you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你根本无法想象，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I can imagine 700 arrows.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我能想象700支箭。

sentences.en: I'm not sure I can imagine 7,000 arrows coming out of the sky.
sentences.zh: 我不太确信自己能否想象7000支箭从天而降的场景。

sentences.en: Maybe 75,000.
I mean, that is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就是那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And they're coming at such a speed.
sentences.zh: 而且它们以极快的速度飞来。

sentences.en: And they, I mean, they're heavy, right?
sentences.zh: 而且它们，我的意思是，它们很重，对吧？

sentences.en: They've got bits of steel or whatever it is on the end and all of that.
sentences.zh: 它们的尖端带有钢片或别的什么东西，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the technology of arrowheads has developed.
sentences.zh: 所以箭头技术已经发展了。

sentences.en: They're much, much, I can't remember exactly why, but it's to do with the weighting and the serration of the arrowhead.
sentences.zh: 它们变得大得多，我记不清具体原因了，但大概与箭头的重量和锯齿有关。

sentences.en: It means that they are much more lethal in the effects, as of course, Henry knows.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们的杀伤效果要大得多，正如亨利自然也知道的那样。

sentences.en: And Henry, unlike Percy at the Battle of Shrewsbury, has made sure that there are plentiful supplies of arrows.
sentences.zh: 而亨利与在什鲁斯伯里战役中的珀西不同，他确保了充足的箭矢供应。

sentences.en: The English can just keep firing and firing and firing.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人可以不断地射击、射击、再射击。

sentences.en: And you have knights who are knocked off into the mud, or you have horses that are shot.
sentences.zh: 你会看到骑士被击落陷入泥潭，或者战马被射中。

sentences.en: Wounded horses start kind of careering around, maybe charging back into the battle line behind them or impaling themselves on stakes.
sentences.zh: 受伤的战马开始横冲直撞，或许会冲回它们身后的战线，或者把自己刺死在木桩上。

sentences.en: I mean, absolutely hideous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，简直惨绝人寰。

sentences.en: And amazingly, the casualties among the horsemen themselves seem to have been relatively light.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，骑兵自身的伤亡似乎相对较轻。

sentences.en: And a lot of them just kind of crawl their way out of the mud and draw, and they're later charged with cowardice.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人只是艰难地从泥潭里爬出来逃走，后来却被指控为懦夫。

sentences.en: But the impact of the failure of their charge to reach the archers is most devastating on the men at arms who were drawn up behind them and who are now advancing in turn.
sentences.zh: 但他们冲锋未能接近弓箭手的失败，对那些排在他们身后、如今正依次推进的重装步兵造成了最具毁灭性的影响。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that they have churned up the ground.
sentences.zh: 原因就在于他们把地面搅得一团糟。

sentences.en: They've got frightened horses knocking into them.
sentences.zh: 受惊的战马撞向他们。

sentences.en: And the combination of this means that it is really, really difficult for them to advance towards the line of English.
sentences.zh: 这些因素结合在一起，意味着他们很难向英格兰人的防线推进。

sentences.en: And all the time, the arrows are still raining down on them.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，箭雨仍在不断倾泻在他们身上。

sentences.en: And is it true, which is what I read as a boy, that when you fall down in this mud, this sort of Paschendaele, the Battle of the Somme scene, this quagmire, that if you fall down
sentences.zh: 我小时候读到过，说当你在这种泥泞中摔倒，这种类似帕斯尚尔、索姆河战役场景的泥潭里，如果你摔倒了

sentences.en: in your armour, your armour is so heavy that you can't get up again.
sentences.zh: 穿着盔甲，你的盔甲太重以至于无法再站起来，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 那是真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and if the mud is of a sufficient liquidity in due course, there's a serious chance that you will drown if you can't move.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果泥浆在适时达到足够的流动性，如果你无法动弹，你将面临严重的溺水危险。

sentences.en: So it's pretty hideous.
sentences.zh: 所以这相当可怕。

sentences.en: And the time it takes for the French men at arms to reach the English line, if it was solid ground, it would be no time at all.
sentences.zh: 法国重装步兵到达英格兰防线所需的时间，如果是坚实的地面，根本花不了多少时间。

sentences.en: But because the ground is so churned up, because there are all these horses rushing everywhere,
sentences.zh: 但因为地面被搅得稀烂，因为到处都是奔跑的战马，

sentences.en: because the arrows are falling, because they have to keep their eyes lowered to ensure that they don't get hit through the visor or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为箭雨纷飞，因为他们必须低着头以确保面甲等部位不会被击中。

sentences.en: It takes them maybe five to ten minutes to cross the gap.
sentences.zh: 他们可能需要五到十分钟才能穿过这段距离。

sentences.en: And by the time they reach the English lines, those who do manage to reach the English lines, I mean, they are shattered.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达英格兰防线时，那些设法到达英格兰防线的人，我的意思是，他们已经筋疲力尽了。

sentences.en: Their armour is very, very heavy.
sentences.zh: 他们的盔甲非常非常重。

sentences.en: And to be slopping through all this kind of hideous, thick, viscous mud, they are completely exhausted by the time they reach the English line.
sentences.zh: 在又厚又浓、粘稠可怕的泥浆中跋涉，当他们到达英格兰防线时，已经彻底精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: And adding to the quality of nightmare that they must have found themselves in, they are being funneled.
sentences.zh: 更增添他们所处噩梦般境况的是，他们正被逼入狭窄的漏斗地带。

sentences.en: Because remember, the trees draw in towards the English line, and they're being shot at from the wings.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，树林向英格兰防线收拢，他们正从两侧遭受射击。

sentences.en: So the instinctive reaction, no matter how brave you are, of course, is to bunch up away from the two sides in the middle.
sentences.zh: 所以出于本能的反应，无论你多么勇敢，当然是挤向中间，避开两侧。

sentences.en: And then on top of that, remember, Henry has this crown, he has his banner, he's situated himself in the middle, he is offering himself up as bait.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，记住，亨利戴着王冠，打着旗帜，把自己置于中央，他把自己当成了诱饵。

sentences.en: He's saying, come and get me.
sentences.zh: 他是在说，来抓我呀。

sentences.en: And so the consequence of this is the French lines are so tightly compressed that it's very difficult for many of them even to raise their arMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，其结果是法军阵型被压缩得如此紧密，以至于许多人甚至很难抬起手臂。

sentences.en: And even if they do have room to raise their arms, many of them are so exhausted by this point that they can't really move.
sentences.zh: 即便他们有空间抬起手臂，他们中的许多人此时也已经精疲力竭，根本无法动弹。

sentences.en: So this becomes your classic crush, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这就变成了典型的踩踏，对吧？

sentences.en: They're in a crush in the middle in the mud.
sentences.zh: 他们挤在中间的泥地里。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, the arrows are raining down on them all the time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，箭雨一直在他们头上倾泻。

sentences.en: And ahead of them, they've got blokes with no trousers on who are soiling themselves.
sentences.zh: 在他们前方，是一群没穿裤子、吓得大小便失禁的家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah, avoiding their bowels left, right and centre.
sentences.zh: 是的，吓得屁滚尿流。

sentences.en: And of course, the winds are gusting, so it's spraying into their face.
sentences.zh: 当然，风势很大，所以这些东西都溅到了他们脸上。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of chemical warfare at its worSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，这可以说是最糟糕的化学战了。

sentences.en: And so with all of these horrors manifesting themselves on the battlefield, I think it is really impressive that actually enough French men at arms reach the English line, that the
sentences.zh: 随着战场上所有这些恐怖景象的显现，我认为真的令人印象深刻的是，居然有足够多的法国重装步兵到达了英格兰防线，以至于

sentences.en: crunch is pretty pulverising.
sentences.zh: 那场碰撞极具毁灭性。

sentences.en: Tom, it's lovely that you're being so generous to the French.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你对法国人如此慷慨，真是太好了。

sentences.en: So I talked about the two previous moments of excruciating peril faced by Henry's army, the Somme and when they advance.
sentences.zh: 所以我之前谈到了亨利军队面临的两次极度危险的时刻，索姆河之战以及他们推进的时候。

sentences.en: This is the third.
sentences.zh: 这是第三次。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Because remember, there are only a thousand English men at arMs.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，英格兰重装步兵只有一千人。

sentences.en: It's a very thin line.
sentences.zh: 这是一条非常薄弱的防线。

sentences.en: And if that line had broken, Henry would still have lost the battle.
sentences.zh: 如果这条防线被突破，亨利依然会输掉这场战役。

sentences.en: The French would have redeemed triumph from seeming disaster.
sentences.zh: 法国人本可以从看似灾难的局面中挽回胜利。

sentences.en: But the English line holds.
sentences.zh: 但英格兰防线守住了。

sentences.en: So you were saying, sorry, I interrupted you.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说，抱歉，我打断了你。

sentences.en: There was a huge crunch and they drive the English back a bit, don't they?
sentences.zh: 有一场巨大的碰撞，他们把英格兰人逼退了一段距离，对吗？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So it's like a kind of rugby scrum, I guess, kind of smashing into a much weaker, smaller scrum, kind of pushes it back.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像英式橄榄球的争球，我猜，猛烈撞击一个弱得多、小得多的争球阵型，把对方撞退了。

sentences.en: But then the English line holds.
sentences.zh: 但随后英格兰防线守住了。

sentences.en: And it's the fact the English line holds that makes the English victory possible.
sentences.zh: 正是英格兰防线的坚守，使得英格兰人的胜利成为可能。

sentences.en: And Henry's chaplain, who is at the back, you know, he's a non-competent, but he's close enough.
sentences.zh: 亨利的随军牧师当时在后方，你知道，他是非战斗人员，但离得够近。

sentences.en: He can see what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他能看清发生了什么。

sentences.en: I mean, he's full of praise for this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对此大加赞赏。

sentences.en: He wrote later, never, it seemed to our older men, had Englishmen ever fallen upon their enemies more boldly and fiercely or with a better will.
sentences.zh: 他后来写道，在我们的老兵看来，英格兰人从未如此勇敢、凶猛或带着如此高昂的斗志向敌人发起进攻。

sentences.en: And so the melee is incredibly ferocious.
sentences.zh: 所以混战极其残酷。

sentences.en: But the English, amazingly, despite being so outnumbered, have the advantage for all the reasons that we've discussed.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊奇的是，尽管寡不敌众，由于我们讨论过的所有原因，英格兰人占了上风。

sentences.en: The arrows are still falling down.
sentences.zh: 箭雨仍在落下。

sentences.en: The French are compacted.
sentences.zh: 法国人阵型紧缩。

sentences.en: They're exhausted.
sentences.zh: 他们筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: And of course, also what is starting to happen is the great piles of bodies are starting to mount up, particularly in front of the position of the king, because all the French
sentences.zh: 当然，开始发生的情况是，大量的尸体开始堆积起来，特别是国王阵地的前方，因为所有的法国

sentences.en: lords want to have a crack at him.
sentences.zh: 贵族都想跟他过两招。

sentences.en: Gloucester, his youngest brother, Humphrey, he's never fought in a battle before.
sentences.zh: 格洛斯特，他最小的弟弟亨弗里，以前从未参加过战斗。

sentences.en: He is bloodied when a sword is jabbed through his groin.
sentences.zh: 当一把剑刺穿他的腹股沟时，他负伤流血了。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 我的天啊。

sentences.en: King stands over him, defending his brother, you know, absolute scenes.
sentences.zh: 国王站在他上方，保护他的弟弟，你懂的，绝对震撼的场景。

sentences.en: Part of his crown is hacked off.
sentences.zh: 他王冠的一部分被砍掉了。

sentences.en: So they really are going after the king.
sentences.zh: 所以他们真的是冲着国王来的。

sentences.en: But actually, the main focus of the French line seems to have been on the right wing for reasons that are not entirely clear, because York is killed there, 86 of his men with him.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，法军防线的主要攻击方向似乎集中在右翼，原因并非完全清楚，因为约克在那里阵亡，同他一起阵亡的还有他的86名部下。

sentences.en: And this seems to be where the fighting is at its most brutal and hard.
sentences.zh: 这里似乎是战斗最残烈、最艰难的地方。

sentences.en: But it's brutal and hard along the entire length of the battle line.
sentences.zh: 但整条战线上都同样残酷而艰难。

sentences.en: But increasingly, as the minutes turn to hours, effectively, it is becoming a bloodbath, because the French are in no position except to just stand there or perhaps lie there and
sentences.zh: 然而随着时间的推移，分秒变成小时，这实际上变成了一场大屠杀，因为法国人除了站在那里或者躺在那里

sentences.en: be slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 任人宰割之外，别无选择。

sentences.en: And the measure of this is that archers start to sneak out from their positions, from behind their stakes.
sentences.zh: 这方面的写照是，弓箭手开始从他们的阵地、木桩后面悄悄溜出来。

sentences.en: And they have mallets, you know, which they use to hammer in their stakes.
sentences.zh: 他们手里拿着木槌，你知道的，那是用来敲入木桩的工具。

sentences.en: And they use these mallets to knock over the French.
sentences.zh: 他们用这些木槌把法国人敲倒。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of like knocking over a 10 pin with a ball.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像用球击倒保龄球瓶。

sentences.en: And they just, you know, the men at arms just kind of keel over.
sentences.zh: 他们只是，你知道的，重装步兵就这样瘫倒在地。

sentences.en: And then the bowmen will draw out their swords, their daggers, and plunge it in through the eye sockets or through the kind of the gap in the neck.
sentences.zh: 然后弓箭手会拔出他们的剑、匕首，刺入对方的眼窝或颈部的缝隙中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so it's commented of the casualties in this battle that the vast majority perish of wounds to the eyes or to the neck.
sentences.zh: 因此有人评论说，这场战役中的伤亡人员绝大多数都是死于眼睛或颈部的伤口。

sentences.en: And it's at this point that people are drowning, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 也就是在这个时候，人们开始溺水，对吧？

sentences.en: Because in the crush, the crush of bodies, corpses, horses, all the chaos, the mud, Frenchmen
sentences.zh: 因为在拥挤的人群中，拥挤的尸体、战马、所有的混乱和泥泞中，法国人

sentences.en: are falling and just never getting up again because they're being suffocated by the mud and the weight of bodies.
sentences.zh: 不断倒下，再也无法站起来，因为他们被泥浆和尸体的重量窒息了。

sentences.en: And the English realise this.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And this is why they keep knocking them over.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们不断把这些人打翻在地。

sentences.en: So Thomas Walsingham, our friend, the monk in St. Albans, he clearly picking up on eyewitness
sentences.zh: 所以我们的朋友、圣奥尔班斯的修士托马斯·沃尔辛厄姆，他显然是从目击者的

sentences.en: reports and he says, the French stood immobilised whilst our men wrenched axes from their hands and felled them as if they were cattle.
sentences.zh: 报告中得知情况并写道：法国人动弹不得，而我们的人则从他们手中夺过战斧，像砍牛一样把他们砍倒。

sentences.en: And this goes on for three hours, Tom?
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了三个小时吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: It basically goes on for three hours.
sentences.zh: 基本上持续了三个小时。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an enormous, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一场巨大的，是的。

sentences.en: Imagine how exhausting.
sentences.zh: 想象一下有多累人。

sentences.en: It's hideous.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Just the mud, the blood, just awful, awful, awful.
sentences.zh: 只有泥浆，鲜血，简直糟糕透顶，糟糕透顶，糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's hideous and yet somehow oddly rousing.
sentences.zh: 这很可怕，但不知为何又有点让人热血沸腾。

sentences.en: Well, as we'll see, I think even the English are kind of stunned and some of them are distressed by the scale of the slaughter.
sentences.zh: 好吧，正如我们所见，我认为甚至连英格兰人都感到震惊，其中一些人对屠杀的规模感到痛心。

sentences.en: But we're in the final episode.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经到了最后一集。

sentences.en: We'll look at reactions to the battle.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨对这场战役的反应。

sentences.en: But just to finish off the account of the battle itself, basically it's over by one o'clock.
sentences.zh: 但为了结束对战役本身的叙述，基本上到一点钟就结束了。

sentences.en: The flower of French chivalry is either dead or taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 法国骑士精神的精华要么战死，要么被俘。

sentences.en: So the English have taken lots of prisoners.
sentences.zh: 所以英格兰人抓了大量的俘虏。

sentences.en: And Henry seems to have his victory.
sentences.zh: 亨利似乎赢得了他的胜利。

sentences.en: But then there comes one final twist, probably the most controversial moment in Henry's reign, features in Shakespeare's play.
sentences.zh: 但随后迎来了最后一个转折，可能是亨利统治时期最具争议的时刻，这也出现在莎士比亚的戏剧中。

sentences.en: And essentially what happens is that Henry thinks he's won.
sentences.zh: 基本上发生的事情是，亨利认为自己赢了。

sentences.en: And then a cry goes up from the rear that the French are rallying and are about to launch another attack and that they are attacking the wagons.
sentences.zh: 然后后方传来一阵呐喊，称法国人正在重整旗鼓，准备发动另一场进攻，并且他们正在袭击辎重队。

sentences.en: So Henry thinks he's surrounded.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利以为自己被包围了。

sentences.en: And this is a massive crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨大的危机。

sentences.en: It's clear that people have broken in through the wagons and they are making off, you know, with all his treasures.
sentences.zh: 显然有人冲破了辎重车，你知道的，带着他所有的财宝逃跑了。

sentences.en: So his crown.
sentences.zh: 也就是他的王冠。

sentences.en: So not the one on his helmet, but his other one.
sentences.zh: 不是头盔上那个，而是他的另一个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Lots of jewels, a kind of jeweled scepter, sword of state, a piece of the true cross.
sentences.zh: 大量的珠宝，一根镶宝石的权杖，国剑，一块真十字架的碎片。

sentences.en: I mean, terrible for Henry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对亨利来说太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And so Henry thinking, you know, my men are exhausted.
sentences.zh: 因此亨利心想，你知道的，我的部下已经筋疲力尽了。

sentences.en: We're still outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 我们依然寡不敌众。

sentences.en: He gives the very controversial that all the prisoners that have been taken should be killed.
sentences.zh: 他下达了一个极具争议的命令：所有被俘的战俘都必须被处决。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And his men are very reluctant to obey this order, partly because obviously that, you know, for pecuniary reasons, a dead prisoner can pay no ransom.
sentences.zh: 他的手下很不情愿遵从这个命令，部分原因显然是，你知道的，出于金钱方面的考虑，死掉的战俘是付不出赎金的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But also because this is very shocking.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: I mean, undoubtedly they have moral qualms about it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毫无疑问他们在道德上对此有顾虑。

sentences.en: It's against the laws of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 这违背了骑士法。

sentences.en: It's against Christian teaching.
sentences.zh: 这违背了基督教教义。

sentences.en: But Henry does it anyway.
sentences.zh: 但亨利还是这么做了。

sentences.en: And what's amazing is that he's never actually blamed for this by French chroniclers.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，法国编年史家实际上从未因此指责过他。

sentences.en: They seem to have accepted that he did what he had to do.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎接受了他做了他不得不做的事。

sentences.en: He's a hard man.
sentences.zh: 他是个硬汉。

sentences.en: He's a ruthless man.
sentences.zh: 他是个冷酷无情的人。

sentences.en: And he does what he has to do to keep his army going.
sentences.zh: 他做了他必须做的事来维持军队运转。

sentences.en: He has to do it because if they are being attacked from the rear as well, and they have in their
sentences.zh: 他必须这样做，因为如果他们也从后方遭到袭击，并且他们的

sentences.en: midst this kind of, you know, hundreds or whatever of Frenchmen, you know, the Frenchmen will just turn on them as soon as they get the chance.
sentences.zh: 在那种你知道的、有成百上千个法国人的情况下，你知道的，法国人一有机会就会对他们反戈一击。

sentences.en: So they have to get rid of...
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须除掉……

sentences.en: That's his thinking, is it?
sentences.zh: 这是他的想法，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you think about it, if you've got more of the enemy coming frontally, they're coming
sentences.zh: 所以如果你仔细想想，如果有更多的敌军从正面压过来，他们又从

sentences.en: around the rear and you have large bodies of Frenchmen in full armor in your own positions,
sentences.zh: 后方包抄，而你自己的阵地里又有大量身穿重甲的法国人，

sentences.en: then if they all combine, you're just going to be obliterated.
sentences.zh: 那么如果他们联手，你们就会被彻底消灭。

sentences.en: So quote Juliet Barker again.
sentences.zh: 所以再次引用朱丽叶·巴克的观点。

sentences.en: She says this was the only order possible.
sentences.zh: 她说这是唯一可行的命令。

sentences.en: And I think in terms of tactics and strategy, she's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为从战术和战略角度来看，她是正确的。

sentences.en: I mean, morally, it remains a blot on Henry's Escuchin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在道德上，这仍然是亨利纹章上的一个污点。

sentences.en: But I think the context of the time makes it clear why he does it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为当时的背景让人明白了他为什么这么做。

sentences.en: And the irony is, is that actually the rumor wasn't true.
sentences.zh: 而讽刺的是，其实那个传闻并不是真的。

sentences.en: The French are not rallying, and the people who have attacked the baggage train are not soldiers.
sentences.zh: 法军并没有重新集结，袭击辎重队的也不是士兵。

sentences.en: They're probably locals who have seized their chance to, you know, to make off with a crown and a bit of the True Cross and, you know, some jewels and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们可能是一些当地人，抓住了机会，你知道的，想顺走一顶王冠、一块真十字架的碎片，还有，你知道的，一些珠宝之类的东西。

sentences.en: They're just sort of local footpads or something helping themselves to the crown jewels.
sentences.zh: 他们只是某种当地的毛贼之流，顺手牵羊拿走了王室珠宝。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I think they're probably locals who think, well, you know, we've had all our harvest has been absolutely ruined.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想他们大概是当地人，心想，好吧，你知道的，我们的庄稼全都被彻底毁了。

sentences.en: Let's try and get something out of this business.
sentences.zh: 不如试着从这买卖里捞点好处吧。

sentences.en: But obviously, the murder of the prisoners adds to the death toll of the battle, and it adds to the number of magnates who are killed, which for contemporaries is perhaps the most
sentences.zh: 但显然，谋杀战俘增加了这场战役的死亡人数，也增加了被杀贵族的人数，对同时代的人来说，这或许是整场战役中

sentences.en: shocking aspect of the whole battle.
sentences.zh: 最令人震惊的方面。

sentences.en: So they're dead.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都死了。

sentences.en: It becomes clear that there isn't going to be another French attack.
sentences.zh: 很显然，法军不会再发动进攻了。

sentences.en: And the battle ends very formally.
sentences.zh: 这场战役以非常正式的方式结束了。

sentences.en: The French herald approaches Henry, and Henry says, do you accept my victory?
sentences.zh: 法国先驱官走向亨利，亨利说，你接受我的胜利吗？

sentences.en: Have I won?
sentences.zh: 我赢了吗？

sentences.en: And the herald says, yes, you know, we concede.
sentences.zh: 先驱官说，是的，你知道的，我们承认失败。

sentences.en: And then Henry asks, he looks around and he sees a castle rising up over the trees.
sentences.zh: 然后亨利问，他环顾四周，看到一座城堡从树林中拔地而起。

sentences.en: And he says, what is the name of that castle?
sentences.zh: 他说，那座城堡叫什么名字？

sentences.en: What is the name of the village that surrounds it?
sentences.zh: 周围那个村庄叫什么名字？

sentences.en: And he's told that it is Agincourt or actually Agincourt in French.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉他那是阿让库尔，在法语里其实是阿让库尔。

sentences.en: And a Burgundian chronicler reports Henry's reply.
sentences.zh: 一位勃艮第编年史家记录了亨利的回应。

sentences.en: And because, said the king, all battles ought to bear the names of the nearest fortress, village
sentences.zh: 国王说，因为所有的战役都应该以离交战地点最近的堡垒、村庄

sentences.en: or town to the place where they were fought, this battle will now and forever be known as the Battle of Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 或城镇命名，这场战役从今以后永远被称为阿让库尔战役。

sentences.en: Tom, wonderful stuff.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，太精彩了。

sentences.en: Absolutely wonderful stuff.
sentences.zh: 绝对是精彩绝伦。

sentences.en: From this day to the ending of the world, we who did this podcast shall be remembered.
sentences.zh: 从今天直到世界尽头，我们这些做过这期播客的人都会被铭记。

sentences.en: So, everybody, we will return next time for the final episode in this series.
sentences.zh: 所以，各位，我们下期将回归，带来本系列的最后一集。

sentences.en: We'll discuss the casualty figures.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论伤亡数字。

sentences.en: We'll talk about what happens to the people taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论被俘人员的下落。

sentences.en: We'll talk about the aftermath of the battle and Henry's determination to make himself king of France as well as England.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论战后的余波，以及亨利立志让自己成为法兰西兼英格兰国王的决心。

sentences.en: And we will look at what happens at the end of his reign.
sentences.zh: 我们还将回顾他统治末期发生的事情。

sentences.en: And we'll discuss, Tom, we'll have a little chat, won't we, about Henry V's reputation and his legacy and where he stands today?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们要讨论一下，我们会好好聊聊吧，关于亨利五世的名声、他的遗产以及他在今天的地位？

sentences.en: Because I know that some people, perhaps associated with this podcast, have in the past said foolish things about Henry V for which they will be wanting to apologise.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道有些人，或许与这个播客有关的人，过去曾对亨利五世说过愚蠢的话，他们现在一定会想要道歉。

sentences.en: So, on that bombshell, we will see you for the tumultuous and decisive final episode of this series next time.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，我们下期将与大家见面，迎来本系列汹涌澎湃且具有决定性意义的最后一集。

sentences.en: Of course, if you're a member of The Rest is History Club, you hear it now.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你是“历史就是一切”俱乐部的会员，你现在就能听到它。

sentences.en: If you're not, therestishistory.com is the place to go to.
sentences.zh: 如果不是，therestishistory.com 就是你要去的网站。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, au revoir.
sentences.zh: 伴随着这个重磅炸弹，再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
